messages:
IncBot: INCIDENT ALERT: apac1d ingress – elevated 5xx rates (ALB/Envoy). Pager sent to NetOncall and Eng-Platform. Auto-escalation triggered.

NetOncall: on it. initial triage: metrics show 503/502 spike starting 3778001200, currently ~18% error-rate over baseline for apac1d.

Sara: seeing similar on dashboard. most failures look like upstream connection failures, not auth.

Jon: tcp_state on envoy pods? anything in conntrack?

Leo: grabbing logs from envoy in apac1d. tail:```
[envoy][2026-03-15T08:20:05Z] upstream_response_timeout
[envoy][2026-03-15T08:20:06Z] connection_reset_before_response_completed
[envoy][2026-03-15T08:20:06Z] too_many_connections_in_pending_accept
```

Aisha: that last line matches socket backlog overload. ALB target group shows 'Rejected: connection queue full' metrics.

NetOncall: good catch. hypothesis: accept backlog (somaxconn) exhaustion on ingress nodes causing upstream RSTs -> envoy returns 502/503. SYN bursts + some long-lived keepalives pushing queue over.

Maria: customer impact estimate: ~10-25% of requests to hosted API in apac1 region see 5xx, mostly short-lived calls (chat/generation). Billing/rate limits unaffected.

Jon: can we temporarily shift traffic away from apac1d to apac1b using weighted DNS? ops-bot?

OpsBot: DNS change history: weighted shift is allowed, but will take ~60s TTL to propagate and may increase latency for apac customers. Do you want me to initiate a 30% -> 0% gradual shift? (confirm with NetOncall)

NetOncall: yes, do 30%->0% over 2m. while that runs, scale ingress ASG + bump somaxconn on affected hosts. Runbooks: "ingress-socket-backlog".

Leo: scaling ASG now: requested +6 nodes to apac1d-ingress-autoscale group.

Sara: applying sysctl change to kube nodes (readonly dry-run then apply):
```bash
sudo sysctl -w net.core.somaxconn=10240
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_max_syn_backlog=4096
# persist via /etc/sysctl.d/99-socket-tuning.conf
```

Jon: reloading envoy worker processes to pick up new backlog? graceful restart recommended.

NetOncall: performing rolling restart of envoy pods with 30s stagger.

Leo: started restart loop. first batch restarted at 3778001300. logs after restart show backlog warnings dropping.

Maria: product/customer comms: drafting status update. impact + mitigation + ETA. proposed: "We’re seeing elevated 5xx in APAC affecting a subset of requests. Engineers are scaling capacity and applying kernel tuning. We expect progressive improvement in the next 10-20 minutes." Approve?

Aisha: approve, send now with note about possible small latency bump.

NetOncall: OpsBot, start sending status to status.redwood.ai with incident id INC-APAC-3778001234.

OpsBot: status posted.

Leo: metrics: error rate decreased from 18% -> 6% after first restart + sysctl, and down to 2% after scale finished and both restarts completed.

Jon: did we pin down root cause?

NetOncall: root cause tentative: target nodes exhausted accept backlog due to SYN/connection burst from a mobile client update with aggressive keepalive + increased concurrency pattern. ALB queued connections overflowed and returned RST to clients. Envoy surfaced as 502/503. No config change deployed at the time.

Sara: follow-ups: 1) add monitoring alert for pending_accepts > 1000 for egress/ingress nodes, 2) tune ALB target group deregistration delay, 3) rate-limit/mitigate noisy clients via edge WAF rules, 4) include somaxconn bump in bootstrap for apac ingress nodes.

Maria: customer note queued to update with RCA once confirmed.

NetOncall: handing off to Eng-Platform for postmortem and long-term mitigations. Summary: applied kernel tuning + autoscale + rolling restarts + traffic shift. Impact limited to apac1 region, partial request failures, mitigated by 3778001450.

Jon: assigning Eng-Platform ticket EP-3428 and scheduling follow-up postmortem 1h after incident.

Sara: logs and metrics archived to incident bucket s3://redwood-incidents/inc-3778001234/ (envoy logs, kernel traces, alb metrics, dns logs).

NetOncall: closing active pager, leaving incident thread open for postmortem. Great work team :thumbsup:
